about: numbers gpu/orbit's tests use, picked 2026-11-05. the centre is four million suns, a round number near the mass of the black hole at the galactic centre; the orbits' sizes are the test's, not the real ones, since a point mass of that much gives 4 km/s on a circle a kiloparsec out and the galaxy's mass, the next branch's, gives a hundred times that. the circle, the inner circle a parsec out, the ellipse and the line are as orbit's tests have them, with rooms three to five times the kernel's errors measured in 32 bits, which measured.json beside this file records with the commands to rerun them. agree is how closely the kernel must agree with the reference on any star, a thousandth of a kiloparsec and a thousandth more for each kiloparsec of the pass; how well the steps must resolve an orbit before the pass and the end of it are compared, a tenth, the same limit the reference's own energy bound is held under, so one measure gates both (below it the kernel agrees with room to spare, measured.json has the worst share; above it neither integrator resolves the pass, and 32-bit rounding through it grows past any bound); the share of drawn stars a run must have compared, so a gate that let every star out would fail; and the worst share of its room a compared pass may reach, which its two step shares are held under as well, in rooms that follow from the pass's: they must agree with the reference's at the kernel's own step as closely as the distance and the speed they are made of do. the share rooms hold a pass's step shares as orbit's tests do, at the kernel's 32-bit errors: a circle's to a turn's share of its steps and that share squared, the ellipse's to the pericentre's closed form as a share of each. the stars are drawn at any speed, a star at rest included: its share in the motion is nothing, and the room that holds it is the speed room's part, the speed room times the step over the distance, which is finite at rest. layout is the kernel's: a star's six numbers and a pass's four, four bytes each, as the solver must ask the device for them. commands is how many a run of exactly that many commands' steps takes, no more. beyond is a speed no 32-bit float can add to itself, with a span whose steps are a unit each: run back, the star flies off to minus infinity, which is as far off as plus. patience is how long a run of some steps may take before the test calls it endless. heavy is the benchmark's batch, a million stars over a thousand steps, drawn from a seed; heavier is sixteen times the work, four million over four thousand. the two are for timing the catalogue's run; measured.json records what they took. huge is room for more stars than any gpu holds. parity is the share of the reference pull that the kernel pull may be off by at any place, three to five times the worst measured, which is the galaxy field in 32 bits; galaxy is the suns of the hole, the measured mass of sgr a*, as the galaxy tests of orbit have it
